questions.question: Does higher price always mean better quality?
options: No, higher price is not a guarantee of better quality
questions.explanation: Higher price is not a guarantee of better quality. Sometimes higher price is related to the brand, packaging, or advertising rather than the product itself.

questions.question: Chrumko is choosing a pencil at the stationery store for school. The more expensive one has colorful packaging, the cheaper one is simple. What should he try?
options: Buy only the more expensive one
questions.explanation: Chrumko should try both pencils. Often you find that both write equally well and the difference is only in the packaging or brand.

questions.question: When is it worth buying a more expensive item?
options: When it is visibly better quality or lasts longer
questions.explanation: Sometimes the more expensive product is really made from better materials or lasts longer. Then the higher price is worth it.

questions.question: What does Chrumko realize about the pencil?
options: It's not always true that more expensive things are automatically better
questions.explanation: Chrumko realizes that it's not always true that more expensive things are automatically better. Sometimes the difference is only in packaging or brand.

questions.question: Why can two similar things cost different amounts of money?
options: Price is affected by material, production, brand, packaging size, and where the product is sold
questions.explanation: Price is affected by material, production method, brand, package size, and where the product is sold.

questions.question: Chrumko needs a new notebook for school. Where should he look?
options: In several stores and compare prices
questions.explanation: Chrumko should look in several stores and compare prices. The same notebook can cost different amounts in different stores.

questions.question: In the first store, he sees a notebook with nice packaging for a higher price. In another store, he finds a similar one cheaper. What's the difference?
options: The difference is only in the packaging and brand, they have the same number of pages
questions.explanation: Both notebooks have the same number of pages and work equally. The difference is only in packaging and brand.

questions.question: What does Chrumko discover?
options: He has to buy the first
Sometimes it pays to look in multiple places to find a better price
questions.explanation: Chrumko discovers that sometimes it pays to look in multiple places to find a better price for the same or similar product.

questions.question: What is a good purchase?
options: The product works well, lasts, and its price matches what it offers
questions.explanation: A good purchase doesn't mean only low price. What's important is that the product works well, lasts, and its price matches what it offers.

questions.question: Chrumko wants to buy a new water bottle. He sees a very cheap plastic one, but it's thin and fragile. Next to it is a stronger one for more money. What should he do?
options: Buy the cheap one because it's cheaper
Choose the stronger one because he'll use it every day
Ask for the most expensive one
questions.explanation: Chrumko should choose the stronger bottle because he'll use it every day and it will serve him longer.

questions.question: Is a cheap bottle a good purchase if it breaks quickly?
options: No, it's not a good purchase if it breaks
questions.explanation: A cheap item that breaks quickly is not a good purchase. On the other hand, an item we use frequently and for a long time might be a good purchase even if it costs more.

questions.question: After a few weeks, is Chrumko happy with his bottle choice?
options: Because it hasn't broken and still works well
questions.explanation: Chrumko is happy because the bottle hasn't broken and still works well. That was a good investment.

questions.question: Why is it worth comparing prices?
options: It helps you decide more wisely and often save money
questions.explanation: Comparing prices helps you decide more wisely and often save money. Even small savings add up over multiple purchases.

questions.question: Chrumko wants to buy pastel colors in the stationery store. He finds a set he likes. What should he do?
questions.explanation: Chrumko should look in other stores too. The same pastels can be cheaper elsewhere.

questions.question: In another store, Chrumko finds the same pastels cheaper. What should he do?
options: Buy them in the first store
Buy the pastels at the better price
questions.explanation: Chrumko decides to buy the pastels at the better price. That way he'll have money left for other school supplies.

questions.question: What is the benefit of comparing prices?
options: You can save money and have more money for other things
questions.explanation: By comparing prices, you can save money and have more money for other things you need or want.

questions.question: What is unit price?
options: How much one piece, one liter, or one gram costs
questions.explanation: Unit price shows how much one piece, one liter, or one gram costs. This helps compare different package sizes.

questions.question: Is a larger package always more expensive?
options: No, a larger package might be better value
questions.explanation: Sometimes a larger package costs more money upfront, but works out better value when you look at the unit price.

questions.question: Chrumko wants to buy water before a trip. He sees two small bottles and one large one. At first he thinks two small ones are better. What does he realize?
options: Two small ones are always better
Two small ones together cost more than one large one
questions.explanation: When he looks more carefully, Chrumko realizes that two small bottles together cost more than one large bottle.

questions.question: How does Chrumko realize which is better value?
options: By the price on the label
His mom shows him that the large bottle has more water for a better price
questions.explanation: His mom shows him that the large bottle has more water for a better price. Chrumko understands that sometimes it's worth looking at the amount too.

questions.question: What is a store?
options: A place where music is only played
A place where buying and selling of items comes together
questions.explanation: A store is a place where buying and selling come together. The store buys products and then offers them to customers.

questions.question: What is included in the price of a product in a store?
options: The item itself, transportation, storage, workers, and store operations
questions.explanation: The price includes costs for transportation, storage, store staff, and running the store.

questions.question: Why might the same product not cost the same everywhere?
options: Because different stores have different costs and prices
questions.explanation: The same product might not cost the same everywhere because different stores have different costs for transportation, storage, and operations.

questions.question: How does payment work in a store?
options: At the checkout, products are scanned, each is added to the total price, and you pay
questions.explanation: At the checkout, products are scanned and the total appears on the screen. This is how the store exchanges money for goods.

questions.question: What is a discount?
options: A price reduction from the original amount
questions.explanation: A discount means that a product costs less than before. Stores use them to attract customers.

questions.question: Does a discount mean you have to buy something?
options: No, a lower price doesn't mean you need the item
questions.explanation: If someone buys something just because it's on sale, they might spend money on something they wouldn't have chosen otherwise.

questions.question: Chrumko goes to the store to buy a snack. He sees a discount on chocolate. What should he do?
options: Think about whether he really needs it and wants it
questions.explanation: Chrumko realizes he didn't plan to buy candy and he has other sweets at home. He decides not to spend the money.

questions.question: Is this a good discount for Chrumko?
options: No, it's not a good deal because Chrumko doesn't need it
questions.explanation: For Chrumko it's not a good deal because he doesn't need the candy. A good discount is only on something you really want and need.

questions.question: Why do stores use colorful signs and large letters?
options: To make products look more interesting and catch our attention
questions.explanation: Stores use colorful signs and large letters to make products look more interesting and catch our attention.

questions.question: Chrumko notices a large yellow sign in the store saying 'best value package at the best price'. What should he do?
options: Look at the actual price and compare with other products
questions.explanation: Chrumko should look at the actual price and compare it with other products. A large sign doesn't automatically mean the best purchase.

questions.question: What does Chrumko discover about this product?
options: The difference is very small or there's another similar product even cheaper
questions.explanation: Looking more carefully, Chrumko discovers that the difference is very small or there's another similar product at an even better price.

questions.question: What does Chrumko learn?
options: A large sign doesn't automatically mean the best purchase
questions.explanation: Chrumko understands that a large sign doesn't automatically mean the best purchase. You need to properly compare prices.

questions.question: What is an impulse purchase?
options: A quick purchase without planning and thinking
questions.explanation: An impulse purchase is buying something quickly without planning and thinking about whether you really need it.

questions.question: Chrumko goes with his mom to the store to buy milk. At the entrance, he sees a cool video game. He immediately wants to buy it. What is this?
options: An impulse purchase - he didn't plan to buy it
questions.explanation: This is an impulse purchase because Chrumko didn't plan to buy a video game, he suddenly wanted it when he saw it.

questions.question: What does his mom tell him?
options: First remember why you came to the store and what you budgeted for
questions.explanation: His mom reminds him that he came for milk and this water bottle is not in the budget. They should first finish their planned shopping.

questions.question: What does Chrumko learn?
options: It's smart to plan what you're going to buy before entering the store
questions.explanation: Chrumko learns that it's smart to make a list of what you need before going to the store so you don't spend money on unplanned things.
